'''Ole Siggaard-Andersen''' (born 10 December 1932) is a Danish physician [[clinical chemistry|clinical chemist]] who elucidated much [[acid base physiology]]. He jointly invented the concepts of [[base excess]] and [[standard base excess]].<ref>{{cite journal
| last        = Siggaard-Andersen
| first       = Ole
|author2=Engel K
| year        = 1960
| title       = A new acid-base nomogram. An improved method for the calculation of the relevant blood acid-base data. 
| journal     = Scan J Clin Lab Invest
| volume      = 12
| issue = 2
| pages       = 177–86
| pmid        = 13848805
| doi         = 10.3109/00365516009062420
}}</ref>

His doctoral thesis, ''The Acid-Base Status of the Blood'', was published as a book for five editions and in five languages.<ref name="aacc">{{Cite web |url=http://www.aacc.org/about/awards/hall_of_fame/Pages/OleSiggaard-Andersen2003UA.aspx |title=Ole Siggaard-Andersen, PhD |access-date=2009-09-21 |archive-date=2009-06-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090621181306/http://www.aacc.org/about/awards/hall_of_fame/Pages/OleSiggaard-Andersen2003UA.aspx |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was honored by the American Association for Clinical Chemistry who awarded him the Edwin F. Ullman Award in 2003.<ref name="aacc" />
